name: Checkout Card-Skimming Compromise
description: Malicious script injected into the online checkout harvests payment cards for weeks before detection, triggering PCI forensics, fines, and reissuance costs.
asset: Online checkout and customer payment data
effect: Card data exposure and PCI penalties
assumptions: Skimming persists undetected for two to eight weeks; exposure scales with checkout volume.
Primary loss covers forensics, card-brand assessments, and remediation.
Secondary loss covers churn, chargeback disputes, and processor relationship damage.

name: Customer Account Takeover Wave
description: Credential-stuffing campaigns replay breached passwords against customer accounts, draining stored value and loyalty points and abusing saved cards.
asset: Customer accounts, stored payment methods, and loyalty balances
threat: Credential-stuffing operators with breached password lists
assumptions: A campaign counts as a loss event when it defeats rate-limiting and takes over accounts at scale.
Primary loss covers fraud reimbursement and support surge per successful campaign.
Secondary loss covers customer churn and payment-provider scrutiny after visible waves.

name: DDoS During Holiday Peak
description: Volumetric and application-layer floods hit the storefront during the highest-revenue trading days, degrading checkout until mitigation engages.
assumptions: Attempts concentrate around promotional events; loss counts only user-visible degradation.
Primary loss is margin on abandoned carts during the outage window, not full revenue.
Secondary loss covers ad spend wasted on unreachable landing pages and SLA credits.

name: Ransomware Halts Fulfillment
description: Ransomware encrypts warehouse management and order routing; orders queue while systems are rebuilt and backlog is cleared by hand.
assumptions: Storefront stays up; the loss is fulfillment downtime, expedited shipping, and rebuild labor.
Backups restore within days; no ransom payment is modeled.
Secondary loss covers refunds, marketplace penalties, and seller-rating damage.

name: Third-Party Plugin Supply-Chain Breach
description: A compromised analytics or personalization plugin ships malicious code into the storefront, exposing session data across every page it loads on.
asset: Storefront third-party integrations and session data
threat: Supply-chain attacker compromising a SaaS plugin vendor
assumptions: Frequency reflects the count of third-party scripts with checkout-page access.
Primary loss covers emergency plugin removal, forensics, and notification mechanics.
Secondary loss covers regulatory exposure and churn tied to disclosed session data.
